name: Harold Levin
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember learning to wait on the doorstep without apologizing.” Thursday often includes a stop at Lighthouse Cove, where Harold takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I am keeping a single slipper by the front door. It reminds my family to wait until I have both feet under me.
appearance: Harold has an aquiline nose and a square chin. Look for iron-gray waves. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a striped cotton shirt with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. In conversation Harold counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Harold always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Harold is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To let the family wait until the wearer is steady.
family: Erin Hubbard is Harold’s younger relative by marriage. Harold sets the time to leave. Erin picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The pawned trumpet*, Erin says, “I recognized that bent third valve from downstairs.”
connections: Irene Franco. A barefoot loan gets a patient home to a family prepared to wait at the door.

reactions.situation: A visitor offers shoes that are far too large
reactions.response: Harold offers to look for a usable pair before anyone is asked to walk in loose shoes.
